messages:
sam_r: Heads-up, ran a focused nsys + perfetto matrix to compare pinned vs pageable behavior after the new batching heuristic landed. posting quick notes + traces.

sam_r: Repro commands i used (pinned vs pageable runs):
```
# instrumented sweep
FORCE_PINNED=1 ./bin/kv_prefetch_workload --qps=400 --duration=300 
sudo nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx --trace=cuda,osrt -o traces/prefetch_pinned_$RUNID
# pageable run
FORCE_PINNED=0 ./bin/kv_prefetch_workload --qps=400 --duration=300
sudo nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx --trace=cuda,osrt -o traces/prefetch_pageable_$RUNID
```

sam_r: TL;DR findings:
- Pinned-only: fewer but larger H2D DMA ops, higher sustained throughput, fewer ~1ms stalls.
- Pageable-only: many small H2Dops, frequent short stalls (0.7-1.4ms) aligned with host staging.
- With the new batch classifier (threshold 0.65) we see avg batch size drop ~15% vs baseline 0.8, which increases tiny peercopy count.
- NVLink peer copies dominate latency when concurrent peercopy_count > 10; they appear serialized in the H2D engine windows.

elaine: Can you paste the perfetto slice around the worst tail? want H2D queue vs kernel launches.

sam_r: perfetto view: https://perfetto.dev/trace/viewer?query=prefetch_matrix_1973500000 (uploaded to traces/prefetch_matrix_1973500000.qdrep)

sam_r: nvprof / nsys aggregated snippet (pinned vs pageable diff):
```
# pageable run (summary)
memcpy HtoD           calls  2,810  total 3.1s  avg 1.1ms
peercopy_async        calls    960  total 2.6s  avg 2.7ms
prefetch_kernel       calls  5,020  total 4.4s  avg 0.9ms

# pinned run (summary)
memcpy HtoD           calls  1,120  total 2.8s  avg 2.5ms
peercopy_async        calls    420  total 1.3s  avg 3.1ms
prefetch_kernel       calls  3,110  total 3.0s  avg 1.0ms
```

sam_r: Key observation: pageable run has ~2.5x memcpy calls vs pinned. many tiny host->device ops show up as lots of small memcpy launches (kernel scheduler overhead visible in perfetto).

ben_platform: That matches what we saw in staging. The classifier mapping small buffers -> "small memcpy kernel" plus host-register fallback yields many staged copies. Did you log allocation type distribution?

sam_r: yes, instrumented runtime report:
```
alloc_summary: cudaHostAllocPinned: 61%
alloc_summary: cudaHostRegister: 22%
alloc_summary: pageable_cpu: 17%
avg_batch_size: baseline(0.8)=11.6  new(0.65)=9.8
```

devon_s: Node topology? NVLink / PCIe layout matters a lot here. where did you run?

sam_r: Mixed config: 8xA100 host, NVLink pairs (0-1,2-3,4-5,6-7), PCIe uploads from host. In perfetto you can actually see H2D PCIe transfers interleaving with NVLink peercopy bursts when KV prefetch kicks off.

sam_r: I also filtered nsys to just memcpy/peercopy/prefetch to compute engine occupancy. exports uploaded: traces/nsys_prefetch_filtered_1973500000.qdrep

sam_r: Measured during a high-burst window: instantaneous H2D throughput ~5.8 GB/s but effective aggregate throughput drops to ~3.2 GB/s due to serialization and kernel launch overhead.

elaine: So two levers: prefer pinned allocations (if customers can tolerate headroom) or change classifier to coalesce small memcpy ops into a single batched hostcopy. Which is easier short-term?

sam_r: Short-term: coalesce prefetches within a small time window (10-20us) into one hostcopy and one DMA submit; that reduces memcpy call count. mid-term: tweak classifier thresholds to prefer the larger memcpy kernel for sizes ~<XKB.

ben_platform: I'll hold the 0.65 rollout. we need the pinned vs pageable matrix diff and the synthetic 500 qps steady-state run. If tail latency reg >10% we revert.

perf-bot: Test matrix results for run 1973500000 uploaded: https://ci.redwood.ai/results/1973500000 (artifacts: traces, metrics.csv, perfetto links)

sam_r: Next steps I will take this sprint:
- Implement coalescing patch for prefetch oplets and run the same matrix.
- Add NVTX markers around coalesce boundary and peercopy submits to capture finer granularity.
- Re-run with forced allocation modes and produce a diff report.

elaine: Sounds good. @ben_platform let's keep rollout paused until we have the coalesce + matrix.

ben_platform: ack :+1:

sam_r: If anyone wants direct access to traces folder ping me, i'll add you. I also left a short perfetto bookmark list in the trace notes for the worst 3 windows.
